classification.difficultyReason: Factor quadratic expressions in trigonometric ratios, reject impossible roots and find every angle in the specified domain; part c first requires the Pythagorean identity.

answer.short:
$\theta=60^\circ,\ 300^\circ$.

Factor the quadratic and reject the root outside the range of cosine.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2\cos^2\theta+3\cos\theta-2&=0\\(2\cos\theta-1)(\cos\theta+2)&=0\end{align*}$$
Thus $\cos\theta=\tfrac12$ or $\cos\theta=-2$. Reject $\cos\theta=-2$, since $-1\le\cos\theta\le1$.
The related angle is $60^\circ$. Cosine is positive in the first and fourth quadrants, so
$$\theta=60^\circ,\ 360^\circ-60^\circ=300^\circ.$$

answer.short:
$\theta=30^\circ,\ 150^\circ$.

Factor the quadratic and reject the root outside the range of sine.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2\sin^2\theta+5\sin\theta-3&=0\\(2\sin\theta-1)(\sin\theta+3)&=0\end{align*}$$
Thus $\sin\theta=\tfrac12$ or $\sin\theta=-3$. Reject $\sin\theta=-3$, since $-1\le\sin\theta\le1$.
The related angle is $30^\circ$. Sine is positive in the first and second quadrants, so
$$\theta=30^\circ,\ 180^\circ-30^\circ=150^\circ.$$

Using $\cos^2\theta=1-\sin^2\theta$:
$$\begin{align*}-2(1-\sin^2\theta)+\sin\theta+1&=0\\2\sin^2\theta+\sin\theta-1&=0\\(2\sin\theta-1)(\sin\theta+1)&=0\end{align*}$$
Thus $\sin\theta=\tfrac12$ or $\sin\theta=-1$.
For $\sin\theta=\tfrac12$, the related angle is $30^\circ$ and sine is positive in quadrants I and II, giving $\theta=30^\circ$ or $150^\circ$.
For $\sin\theta=-1$, $\theta=270^\circ$.
Hence $\theta=30^\circ,\ 150^\circ,\ 270^\circ$.
